title: Presentable approximations of a fixed cellular tree with compatible supports
statement:
Use the universe, regularity, presentability, weak saturation and $L$-tree definitions in [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation]. Let $\tau$ be uncountable regular and let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary locally $\tau$-presentable category with small Hom sets: it has all small colimits and is generated under small $\tau$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $L$ be an arrow class in $\mathcal A$. Fix a $\tau$-good $L$-tree with root $X$, small indexing poset $T$, and specified attaching arrows $P_t\to Q_t$ in $L$. No weak-equivalence class is part of these data.

There exist a small $\tau$-filtered poset $P$, an inclusion-increasing family of downward-closed subsets $S_p\subseteq T$ with $|S_p|<\tau$, and a diagram $p\mapsto h_p:M_p\to N_p$ in the arrow category, with $\tau$-presentable endpoints, satisfying the following properties. Each $h_p$ is the colimit arrow of an $L$-tree on $S_p$ with root $M_p$ and the specified attaching arrows indexed by $S_p$. There are compatible root maps $M_p\to X$ and isomorphisms from the objectwise pushouts of these trees along $M_p\to X$ to the original restricted trees on $S_p$. For $p\leq p'$, the transition square of arrows extends to maps between the trees on the common cells, respecting root maps, predecessor colimit maps and both legs of every specified attaching square, with the identity on $P_t$ and $Q_t$; these maps compose and the pushout identifications are compatible with them. The resulting cocone $h_p\to(X\to Y_T)$ is colimiting in the arrow category. For every $E\subseteq T$ with $|E|<\tau$, there is $p\in P$ with $E\subseteq S_p$.

For every nonempty filtered subposet $Q\subseteq P$ in its inherited order, put $S_Q=\bigcup_{q\in Q}S_q$, $M_Q=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}M_q$, $N_Q=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}N_q$, and let $h_Q:M_Q\to N_Q$ be the arrow colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The arrow $h_Q$ is the colimit arrow of an $L$-tree on $S_Q$ with root $M_Q$ and the specified attaching arrows indexed by $S_Q$. The canonical square with top arrow $h_Q$, bottom arrow $X\to Y_{S_Q}$ and left leg $M_Q\to X$ is a pushout. In particular $h_Q$ lies in the weakly saturated closure of $L$.
